To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the beliefs that family caregivers have about filial obligation are related to their satisfaction and burden.
the beliefs about filial obligations and parental dependency that are held by family caregivers are associated with their satisfaction and burden.

(a) caregivers’ beliefs about the nature of filial obligation and the extent of parental dependency influence the extent to which they experience caregiver satisfaction and burden, (b) the beliefs that influence caregiver satisfaction and burden are different, and (c) caregiver beliefs about the extent of parental dependence and the nature of filia obligation can be assessed reliably.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement of caregivers’ beliefs, and the implications of these beliefs for caregivers and the families they care for.
the development of reliable and valid measures of caregivers’ beliefs, and the implications for understanding caregivers’ satisfaction and burden.
the conceptualization and assessment of caregiver ideology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the study of filial obligation and caregiver ideology is important because it is a useful lens for understanding the experience of family caregivers and the cultural context in which caregiving occurs.
the caregiver ideology scale is a reliable instrument to measure caregivers’ attitudes towards their caregiving role and their parents’ dependency.
filial obligation and dependency beliefs are important to the caregiver experience and are best assessed by a combination of open and closed-ended items.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
caregiver ideology is an important variable that can be measured and used to understand caregiver behaviour.
the caregiver’s beliefs are a significant factor in the caregiving experience, and that these beliefs are not simply the result of the caregiving experience.
caregiver beliefs about filial obligations and parental dependency can be measured and are useful in understanding caregiver outcomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
beliefs about filial obligations are a key aspect of caregiver ideology and that these beliefs have implications for the caregiver experience.
the study of cultural models can be informed by quantitative methods.
the study of caregiver ideology should not be limited to qualitative inquiry.
